title: Isn't that weird?
author: Enefium
selftext:
https://i.redd.it/e74hwzz0sdyh1.png

We've all experienced this at some point, right?

1) You prompt some idea into existence

2) \[insert your favorite AI agent\] gives you the "We're all set, wow you're so smart to come up with such a nice and creative idea."

3) You ask to debug the code

4) "Here's a list of X bugs, Y exploits, and Z minor inconsistencies/improvements."

And you're telling me the AI agent somehow couldn't figure out those XYZ during the initial implementation? I find that pretty weird. What's different between the initial prompt and the request to debug the code? Seems like a very "human" coding process, where you write your code thinking it's flawless, only to find all the bugs afterward.

How do you all interpret and handle this kind of behavior?

replies.author: Blueberry_Gecko
replies.body: Ah, I got super tripped up by bandwidth. Makes sense, I thought you meant the bandwidth of its "thought stream" or whatever, but you probably just meant the amount of effort.

comments.author: Blueberry_Gecko
comments.body:
Yeah, effort. Just be wary of costs, if you increase effort it can also cause the model to spin in circles on super easy tasks that don't need further iterations at all, and sometimes it will even doubt itself into a wrong solution. If you only ask the correction prompt rarely, it might be better to just have it saved as a text snippet that you can paste in on demand. Depends on how complex the work you ask it to do is. If you find yourself prompting in a "spiky pattern" like trivial thing->massive feature->trivial thing, it's probably better to only raise effort on the massive feature or paste the text snippet there.

There's no hard science to it. If the AI were infinitely perfectly trained, none of the parameters and reprompts would be needed, but we can't have everything :D
